name: Beldum

changes.criterion: Group Pokémon by their dominant body color palette (blue, green, brown/dark, red/orange, yellow/tan), treating mechanical or mineral-bodied Pokémon as a separate category regardless of color. Organic Pokémon with blue tones group together; mechanical/steel Pokémon form their own group.
dimensions: blue_dominance (w=3): How much of the Pokémon's body is dominated by blue or blue-grey organic coloring. 0 = no blue present, 1 = almost entirely blue.
green_dominance (w=3): How much of the Pokémon's body is dominated by green coloring (including yellow-green). 0 = no green present, 1 = almost entirely green.
brown_dark_dominance (w=3): How much of the Pokémon's body is dominated by brown, dark grey, black, or charcoal coloring. 0 = none, 1 = almost entirely these tones.
red_orange_dominance (w=3): How much of the Pokémon's body is dominated by red or orange coloring. 0 = no red/orange, 1 = almost entirely red/orange.
yellow_tan_dominance (w=2): How much of the Pokémon's body is dominated by yellow, tan, cream, or warm beige coloring. 0 = none, 1 = almost entirely these tones.

mechanical_or_mineral (w=4.5): Does the Pokémon appear mechanical, metallic, man-made, or mineral/rock-based rather than biological? 0 = fully organic/biological creature, 1 = clearly mechanical, steel, or constructed appearance.

criterion: Group Pokémon by their dominant body color palette (blue, green, brown/dark, red/orange, yellow/tan), treating mechanical or mineral-bodied Pokémon as a separate category regardless of color. Organic Pokémon with blue tones group together; mechanical/steel Pokémon form their own group.
notes: The feedback strongly indicates item_007 (Bronzong, clearly mechanical) should be separated from item_011 (Beldum, blue organic larva), item_039 (Panpour, organic monkey), item_038 (Oddish, organic plant), and item_034 (Larvitar, organic dinosaur). All the 'closer' items are organic even if they share blue tones. Raising mechanical_or_mineral weight to 4.5 will push item_007 into a mechanical cluster away from organic blue Pokémon. I also added yellow_tan as a dimension to better separate tan-bodied Pokémon, and merged brown/dark to better capture dark-toned organics like Larvitar.

name: Flapple

changes.criterion: Group Pokémon by their dominant body color palette (blue, green/dark, red/orange, yellow/tan), with mechanical or metallic Pokémon as a separate group. Pokémon with complex multi-color patterns or large dark+green bodies group together, separate from small single-color-dominant Pokémon.
dimensions: mechanical_or_mineral (w=5): Does the Pokémon appear mechanical, metallic, man-made, or mineral/rock-based rather than biological? 0 = fully organic/biological creature, 1 = clearly mechanical, steel, or constructed appearance.
blue_dominance (w=3): How much of the Pokémon's body is dominated by blue or blue-grey coloring. 0 = no blue present, 1 = almost entirely blue.

green_dark_dominance (w=3.5): How much of the Pokémon's body combines green with dark brown or black tones as co-dominant colors. 0 = neither green+dark present together, 1 = body is strongly both green and dark/brown simultaneously.
red_orange_dominance (w=3): How much of the Pokémon's body is dominated by red or orange coloring. 0 = no red/orange, 1 = almost entirely red/orange.

yellow_tan_dominance (w=3.5): How much of the Pokémon's body is dominated by yellow, tan, cream, or warm beige coloring, with minimal other colors. 0 = none or mixed with other strong colors, 1 = almost entirely these tones.

color_complexity (w=2): How many distinct strong color regions does the Pokémon's body have? 0 = one dominant color covers nearly the whole body, 1 = three or more clearly distinct color regions each covering significant body area.

criterion: Group Pokémon by their dominant body color palette (blue, green/dark, red/orange, yellow/tan), with mechanical or metallic Pokémon as a separate group. Pokémon with complex multi-color patterns or large dark+green bodies group together, separate from small single-color-dominant Pokémon.
notes: The key new insight: item_030 (red/green/tan dragon) and item_035 (dark brown + green gorilla) should group together and both should be closer to item_007 (mechanical) than to item_019 (tan acorn). item_019 is very tan-dominant with simple coloring. item_030 has high color_complexity and red+green. item_035 has green_dark_dominance. item_007 is mechanical. What separates item_019 from the others is its high yellow_tan_dominance and low color_complexity. By raising yellow_tan_dominance weight and adding color_complexity, item_019 will sit in a tan/simple cluster away from item_030, item_035, and item_007 which all have more complex or dark+green coloring. The mechanical dimension keeps item_007 separate from organic blue Pokémon like item_011.
